title: A Cellar for the Well
premise: Ines Okonkwo, a skeptical property surveyor, is hired to appraise Hollowell House, a decaying estate whose cellar contains a dry well that hums a half-remembered song. The house's mirrors lag one second behind reality, and Ines discovers the house appraises its occupants in return: it measures what they would trade to survive. As the lag widens and previous surveyors' fates surface in the walls, Ines learns the well demands a final verse sung by an heir of the family that dug it — and that their client, Ada Hollowell, is the last heir, planning to sell rather than sing. Ines must convince Ada to face the well, resist singing along themselves, and complete the verse's true ending — silence — before the mirrors catch up and the house swallows them both.
about_author: Lena Kavanagh is the pen name of a former building inspector who spent a decade cataloguing condemned properties across the American Midwest. Their fiction draws on the strange intimacy of measuring rooms no one should live in anymore.

chapters.title: The Commission
chapters.summary: Ines Okonkwo accepts an unusually generous appraisal job on Hollowell House from a terse lawyer representing the reclusive Ada Hollowell. POV: Ines. Beat: professional confidence masking a recent bankruptcy that makes the fee impossible to refuse.

chapters.title: Square Footage
chapters.summary: First walkthrough; Ines measures every room but finds the tape readings disagree with each other by inches that change between visits. POV: Ines. Beat: unease rationalized as settling foundations and bad equipment.

chapters.title: The Dry Well
chapters.summary: In the cellar, Ines finds a stone well, bone-dry, that emits a faint melodic hum when they lean over it. They log it as 'structural anomaly.' POV: Ines. Beat: curiosity overriding instinct.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: At dusk, Ines notices every mirror shows the room a beat behind — their reflection raises a hand after they do. They test it for an hour until the lag closes. POV: Ines. Beat: denial hardening into obsession.

chapters.title: Ada
chapters.summary: Ada Hollowell arrives unannounced, warns Ines never to hum in the house, and refuses to enter the cellar. She reveals her family has owned the house for six generations without selling. POV: alternating Ines/Ada. Beat: wary alliance formed out of mutual fear.

chapters.title: What the House Appraises
chapters.summary: Ines finds appraisal documents in the study listing not values but prices paid: years, names, voices — signed by ancestors. The latest page bears blank lines awaiting a signature. POV: Ines. Beat: horror of realizing the profession has been inverted.

chapters.title: The Song's First Verse
chapters.summary: Sleepless, Ines catches themselves humming the well's tune and stops mid-note; the mirrors' lag jumps to three seconds. Ada confesses the song must be finished by an heir or the house takes payment itself. POV: Ada. Beat: guilt and inherited dread.

chapters.title: Previous Surveyors
chapters.summary: Ines traces four prior appraisers through county records; all vanished mid-contract, their last reports describing the same lagging mirrors. One report ends mid-sentence. POV: Ines. Beat: cold clarity — this is a pattern, not a haunting.

chapters.title: Lag
chapters.summary: The delay spreads beyond mirrors into sound: footsteps echo late, doors close after they're shut. Ines times it — five seconds now, growing daily. POV: Ines. Beat: claustrophobic acceleration.

chapters.title: The Verse Ada Won't Sing
chapters.summary: Ada explains the second verse was sung by her grandmother to buy the family time; the third verse's words were deliberately lost. The house has been 'appraising' ever since, waiting for someone to finish it. POV: Ada. Beat: confession as burden-sharing.

chapters.title: Offer
chapters.summary: The house makes its move: Ines's debts vanish overnight, credit cleared, the fee tripled — payment for services not yet rendered. A mirror shows Ines signing the blank line. POV: Ines. Beat: temptation dressed as relief.

chapters.title: Refusal Has a Sound
chapters.summary: Ines tries to leave; the road loops back to the drive. Every attempt costs seconds off the mirrors' lag — the house counts refusal as interest. POV: Ines. Beat: trapped, pride curdling to terror.

chapters.title: The Cellar at Night
chapters.summary: Ines descends with a recorder and captures the song whole — two verses and a third that sounds like words played backward. Playback later contains their own voice answering. POV: Ines. Beat: the moment belief becomes unavoidable.

chapters.title: Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: Research reveals the well predates the house; the Hollowells were hired generations ago to keep it fed, and 'heir' means warden, not owner. Ada is not the beneficiary — she's the collateral. POV: Ada. Beat: rage at inheritance as servitude.

chapters.title: Singing Along
chapters.summary: A storm traps them both; the house plays the first verse through its own pipes, and Ada nearly joins in before Ines physically silences her. The mirrors jump to nine seconds behind. POV: alternating. Beat: the rule made flesh — learn it, never sing it.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: Ines deciphers the ledger: every 'gift' the house gave them is itemized against their future — years of life, their memory of their mother's face. Survival here is a loan. POV: Ines. Beat: reckoning with what they've already spent.

chapters.title: What Silence Costs
chapters.summary: Ada reveals the lost third verse isn't words at all: the song ends in deliberate silence, held by an heir who stands at the well and refuses to answer it. No Hollowell has managed it. POV: Ada. Beat: hope with a body count attached.

chapters.title: The House Objects
chapters.summary: As they prepare, the house fights back — walls rearrange, the cellar stairs lengthen, mirrors show versions of them who already failed. Ines's recorded voice begins singing from empty rooms. POV: Ines. Beat: the antagonist revealed as architecture.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: They go down together at dawn, Ines carrying the ledger as evidence of debt, Ada carrying nothing. The well's hum is now a chorus of every voice it has taken. POV: alternating. Beat: grim resolve before the threshold.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: At the well's mouth, the song offers Ada the ending in her grandmother's voice. She opens her mouth — and holds silence instead, gripping Ines's hand while the house screams the verse at her. POV: Ada. Beat: climax; will as weapon.

chapters.title: Appraised at Nothing
chapters.summary: The mirrors snap into real time; the ledger burns itself blank; the well exhales once and goes truly silent. The house, valued at nothing owed, begins to settle like a lung deflating. POV: Ines. Beat: release after suffocation.

chapters.title: Final Inspection
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Ines files the appraisal: structure unsound, recommend demolition. Ada signs the sale. On the way out, Ines checks one last mirror — and waits a full second longer than needed. POV: Ines. Beat: survival achieved, vigilance permanent; the price of living through it.
